big_idea: 5 named solids: cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones. Sort by FACES, EDGES, VERTICES.
learning_intention: We are learning to sort 5 named solids by their faces, edges, and vertices.
student_learning_goal: I can sort 5 named solids by faces, edges, and vertices.
success_criteria: I can COUNT faces, edges, and vertices.
I can SORT solids by attribute.
I can EXPLAIN how I sorted.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Trekker Tig and Compass Coco — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Trekker Tig: Geometers, today we meet 5 NAMED solids — cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones. Count their FACES, EDGES, and VERTICES! Tig opens: 'Sort by ATTRIBUTES, not by LOOKS!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Trekker Tig the Tiger Cub puppet with backpack. 'Geometer friends — in Grade 3 we name 5 solids. Each one has a different number of FACES, EDGES, and VERTICES.'

Define. 'A FACE is a FLAT side. An EDGE is the LINE where two faces meet. A VERTEX is a CORNER where edges meet.'

Reveal each solid one by one with the chart:

CUBE: 6 faces (all squares), 12 edges, 8 vertices.
RECTANGULAR PRISM: 6 faces (rectangles), 12 edges, 8 vertices.
SQUARE PYRAMID: 5 faces (1 square + 4 triangles), 8 edges, 5 vertices.
CYLINDER: 2 flat faces (circles) + 1 curved, 2 edges (curved), 0 vertices.
CONE: 1 flat face (circle) + 1 curved, 1 edge (curved), 1 apex vertex.

'Trekker Tig says — every solid has a NAME and a COUNT. Use BOTH!'

Demo. 'I'll pick a solid card and name + count.' Pick a cube. 'CUBE — 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices.'

Then partners get a sorting hoop labelled FACES=6 and 3 solid cards. They check.

Now each pair gets the Solid Card Set (15 cards: 3 of each type). They sort first by NAME (5 piles), then by FACES.

'Trekker Tig says — sorting GROUPS solids by their attribute!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Solid Card Sets. Pairs sort by NAME (5 piles).
Resort by FACES (1 face, 5 faces, 6 faces).
Help with cone (curved counts as 1 face?). Use chart.

GEOMETER'S CHOICE: Pairs INVENT their own sorting rule (by EDGES, curved-vs-flat, tall-vs-short). Two pairs share. Class compares which rule is most useful. Cite van Hiele (1986) Level 2 — children invent property-based classifications.
steps.teacher_prompt: Tig: 'Different rules, different sorts. Pick the rule that helps you.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk to 5 stations, one per solid type. NO-PAPER PATH: children form solid shapes with hands/bodies (fists for cubes, flat hand for square faces). Body becomes the solid.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: names; counts; sorts; explains; consistency.

discussion_prompts: How many faces on a CUBE?
Where's the VERTEX of a CONE?
How are CYLINDER and CONE different?
Tig's preview: tomorrow Coco helps us BUILD with these solids (Lesson 2 — E1.1). What attribute matters when stacking?
consolidation.exit_routine: Tig + Coco refrain — 'Sort by ATTRIBUTES, not by LOOKS — FACES, EDGES, VERTICES!' (3x). Each child writes one solid with attribute counts.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Tracker of solid naming and attribute counts.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 1 sets the baseline for solid identification.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child confuses CYLINDER with CONE — repairing the curved-solid mix-up at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On 3D solid sorting, the trap is van Hiele Level 1 visual fixation: child sorts by appearance (cube looks like a die) rather than properties (faces, edges, vertices). Battista (2007) and van Hiele (1986) frame the L1→L2 transition as the gateway to all later geometry.

Today: sort by named attributes. Tomorrow Lesson 2 composes structures; Lesson 3 congruent faces; Lesson 4 map+move; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Sorting activity. Child puts cone in the cylinder pile.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Trekker Tig asks — where's the POINTY end?'

Probe. 'Cone has a point at the top — that's the APEX vertex. Cylinder has 2 flat circles, no point.'

Generalise. 'Trekker Tig says — POINT = cone. NO POINT = cylinder.'

If still confused: hand both shapes. 'Run finger up the side. Cone narrows to a point. Cylinder stays the same.'
expected_student_responses: (Stretched) 'Both have curved faces but cone has 1 flat face, cylinder has 2.'
common_misconceptions: Cylinder has a point. (Repair: only cone does.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child sorts by appearance: drill 'name the ATTRIBUTE first — faces, edges, vertices'; child re-sorts by named attribute.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can count faces but loses edge count: physical demo with finger-tracing; child counts each edge once.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child sorts but cannot articulate: force 'this solid has ___ faces and ___ edges, so it sorts as ___.'

parts_outline.task: Name 5 solids in a picture row.
Count faces, edges, and vertices for 3 solids.
Sort 8 mixed solids into 5 named piles.
